rdf:Description.dc:description:
The core module of BiDO allows us to describe any entity and the related bibliometric data (through the property `bido:holdsBibliometricDataInTime`) at a certain time (i.e., `tvc:atTime`, a property defined by the imported TVC ontology for specifying temporal instants or intervals) and according to a certain agent (through the property `bido:accordingTo`, which is a sub-property of `prov:wasAttributedTo` and allows us to indicate the agent responsible for such bibliometric data).
![The architecture of the BiDO-Core module.](bido-core.png)
Two alternative kinds of bibliometric data are specifiable (through the property `bido:withBibliometricData`) in BiDO: numeric data and categorial data. Numeric data are those characterised by a certain integer or float value related to a particular bibliometric measure. Some of these measures – i.e., h-index, author citation count, e-index, and journal impact factor – are available in a particular module of BiDO responsible for describing the most common bibliometric measures.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A discrete scale defining the rating given by a reviewer for a specific scientific contribution.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: number of poster paper accepted
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A measure indicating how many poster papers has been accepted for publication/presentation in the venue.
An acceleration point located in the middle of the considered research period.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: median acceleration
has rating value
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value of the rating given to a review.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 10 years beginning
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The interval covering the first 10 years of a research career.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 4 out of 5 (Discrete 1 to 5 review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 4 in a discrete scale from 1 to 5 for review rating.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Accept to Reject, Two Strikes review rating scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Discrete scale from 'Accept' to 'Reject', including pre-screening and two strikes rule.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Medium (Expert to Null reviewer confidence scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 'Medium' in a discrete scale from 'Expert' to 'Null' for rating reviewers' confidence.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: numeric bibliometric data
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Bibliometric data represented by numbers. Such numeric data are those characterised by a certain integer or float value related to a particular bibliometric measure.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Strong Accept (Strong Reject to Strong Accept, without Borderline review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 'Strong Accept' in a scale from 'Strong Reject' to 'Strong Accept' for review rating.
The value 1 in a discrete scale from 1 to 5 for review rating.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 1 out of 5 (Discrete 1 to 5 review rating scale)

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The relation between a value in time and the specific context within which the fact of the entity having the value is relevant.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: within context
10 out of 10 (Discrete 0 to 10 review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 10 in a discrete scale from 0 to 10 for review rating.
A polynomial growth pattern characterizing the slope of the curve.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: polynomial
Strong Reject to Strong Accept review rating scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Discrete scale from Strong Reject to Strong Accept, including Bordeline

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: agent
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: scholarly venue management system
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A venue management system (such as a conference management system, or a journal management system) that can be used for managing scholarly venues.
A review process where the identity of the authors is concealed from the reviewers, and vice versa.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: double blind peer review

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 'High' in a discrete scale from 'Expert' to 'Null' for rating reviewers' confidence.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: High (Expert to Null reviewer confidence scale)
premature acceleration
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: An acceleration point occurring early in the considered research period.
The actual value of the bibliometric data in consideration.

2 out of 10 (Discrete 0 to 10 review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 2 in a discrete scale from 0 to 10 for review rating.

number of short paper accepted

The value 1 in a discrete scale from 0 to 10 for review rating.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 1 out of 10 (Discrete 0 to 10 review rating scale)
Major revision (Accept to Reject, Two Strikes review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 'Major revision' in a discrete scale from 'Accept' to 'Reject, Two Strikes' for review rating.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: peer review type
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A type of of peer review process, such as 'double-blind' or 'open'.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 0 out of 10 (Discrete 0 to 10 review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 0 in a discrete scale from 0 to 10 for review rating.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Discrete -2 to 2 review rating scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Discrete scale from -2 to 2, including 0.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Approved to Not Approved review rating scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Discrete scale from 'Approved' to 'Not Approved', including Aprproved With Reservations.

The relation between the slope and the related strength.

has acceleration point
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The relation between a curve and its acceleration point.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A low strength characterizing the slope of the curve.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: 0 to 5 continuos review rating scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A continuous review rating scale, ranging from 0 to 5.

reviewer confidence scale
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A scale defining the confidence of a reviewer for a given topic.
Any academic event such as conferences, workshops, symposia.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: academic event

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: An index that attempts to measure both the productivity and impact of the published work of a scientist or scholar. The index is based on the set of the scientist's most cited papers and the number of citations that they have received in other publications. The index can also be applied to the productivity and impact of a group of scientists, such as a department or university or country, as well as a scholarly journal.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: h-index

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A category that can be used for ranking a conference according to the related ranking that defines it.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: conference ranking category
A*
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The CORE category for a flagship conference, a leading venue in a discipline area.
The citation interval between 6561 (included) and 19683 (excluded).

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The relation between the value in time situation and the actual value held by the entity partaking in that situation.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: with value

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The citation interval between 729 (included) and 2187 (excluded).

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A review process where the identity of the reviewers is concealed from the authors.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has curve

A scholarly periodical primarily devoted to the publication of original research papers.
rdf:Description.rdfs:label: journal
Accept (Strong Reject to Strong Accept review rating scale)
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The value 'Accept' in a scale from 'Strong Reject' to 'Strong Accept' for review rating.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: value in time
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A particular kind of time-indexed situation that represents a hub linking the entity having a particular value, the value itself and the temporal and contextual extents from which the entity-value relationship depends.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: order of magnitude
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A categorization of the number of citations received in the considered period according to a uniform model of common-sense estimation, which describes intervals of half-order of magnitude - i.e., “[0,1)”, “[1,3)”, “[3,9)”, “[9,27)”, “[27,81)”, “[81,243)”, “[243,729)”, etc.
